persona: Aarav, a product analyst navigating launch stress, exercise habits, and two recurring relationships.

messages.content: I noticed I stopped exercising when work got intense. Why does it hit my mood so hard?

That pattern makes sense: when work pressure rose, the entries show exercise dropping off at the same time mood got heavier. It does not mean exercise is a magic fix, but it does look like one of your steadier supports.

For today, I would treat it gently: choose the smallest version of the habit that still counts, then notice whether your body feels even a little less braced.

metadata.text: Sarah approved the final project plan and said it supports my promotion case. I felt trusted again instead of just evaluated.
The work backlog is real. I did not exercise and I can feel my patience thinning.
I went for a short run anyway. It did not fix work, but my body felt less braced by the end.

messages.content: I am nervous that Sarah's feedback means I am falling behind again.

The Sarah thread looks like it softened over time: earlier feedback landed as criticism, but later entries show clearer planning and trust returning. That suggests the pressure was real, but not the whole relationship.

Before the next feedback moment, it may help to separate the task signal from the self-worth signal: what is she asking you to change, and what does that not say about your competence?

metadata.text: Work was still intense, yet I handled feedback without spiraling. That felt new.
This week feels better. Exercise is back, work is clearer, and I am not carrying everything alone.
No workout again. I scrolled late while worrying about money, slept poorly, and woke up already behind.

messages.content: Maya and I are okay now, but I still feel bad that I disappeared when stressed.

It makes sense that you still feel tender about that. The entries show you pulling back during the hardest stretch, then repairing with Maya through an honest conversation and a walk.

The useful part is not that you handled it perfectly; it is that repair was possible. A small next step could be naming the pattern early, before stress turns into silence.

metadata.text: I still have pressure around the launch, but I can see the pattern now: sleep, exercise, and honest conversations help.
The budget still worries me, but I made a spreadsheet and stopped avoiding the numbers.
Maya and I walked after dinner. We talked about stress without it taking over the whole evening.
